findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections, allowing credentials and data in transit to be intercepted.

findings.issue_category: hard-coded database credentials in user data
findings.description: The instance user_data interpolates the RDS master username and the ${var.password} value directly into a PHP include file written to disk. EC2 user_data is retrievable in plaintext from the instance metadata service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) by any process or SSRF-capable application on the host, and is also visible in the EC2 API/console, leaking the database master password.

No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption settings are specified, so the instance's EBS volume may be created unencrypted (absent account-level default encryption). The volume stores the database credentials file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, so data at rest is unprotected.

No metadata_options block is defined, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with an attached IAM instance profile and a PHP web application reachable from the network, an SSRF in the application can retrieve both the role's temporary credentials and the user_data containing the DB password.

The provisioned web application serves an HTTP-only Apache/PHP site (only httpd is installed and started, with no TLS configuration), so employee name and address form submissions and query results traverse the network in cleartext.
The PHP client connects with mysqli_connect() without any SSL/TLS options or CA certificate, so credentials and query data between the app server and the RDS instance are transmitted unencrypted.

The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the catalog database's underlying storage and snapshots are stored unencrypted. Any compromise of the storage layer or snapshot sharing exposes cleartext data.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing it to internet-wide credential attacks; only the security group stands between the database and the public internet.

The master password is supplied through var.password and the master username is hard-coded to the default 'admin'. Passing the credential through a Terraform variable stores it in cleartext in state (and typically in tfvars/CI configuration), and the predictable 'admin' username aids brute-force attacks against the publicly reachable endpoint.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached via aws_iam_instance_profile.catalog_app_profile to the internet-facing catalog app server, so compromise of that instance yields account-wide control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases (including snapshot creation/restore and DB credential modification) — a direct privilege escalation path.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel if the database host is compromised.
